newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom talks with internet svce providers.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom talks with internet svce providers.

text.p: French telephone company France Telecom has held talks with Internet service providers but these are not commercial negotiations at the moment, a France Telecom spokesman said on Monday.

He was answering questions on an article in Monday's issue of financial daily Les Echos, which said Lagardere Groupe was seeking closer ties between its Club Internet unit and France Telecom's Internet service provider Wanadoo.
No one was immediately available to comment at Lagardere.

Les Echos said the recent Internet boom in France was prompting Lagardere, which has not yet forged an alliance for its Internet service provider and other multimedia interests, to seek a partnership with a telecommunications operator.
"Initially the talks should concern a link between the on-line service Club Internet and France Telecom's Internet access service, Wanadoo," Les Echos said.
Internet service providers want telecommunications operators to share technical costs and to help the development of Internet use in France, the France Telecom spokesman said.
"Everyone is talking to everyone in this field... Matra Hachette (Lagardere Group) are talking too," he said.
"But these are meetings, dialogues, not commercial talks or negotiations," he said.
Les Echos said Arnaud Lagardere, the son of Lagardere Group chairman Jean-Luc Lagardere, had recently opened discussions with France Telecom to look at possible partnerships.

"We are prepared to look at a link between Club Internet and Wanadoo. The problem all on-line services have is to see how they can minimise network costs," Les Echos quoted a France Telecom executive as saying.
